title: MBOX import
blurb: Choose the Import MBOX icon button beside Local Folders in the account list to review 1–20 exported or stopped mailbox files (including Thunderbird extensionless files), an existing or new local destination, and mboxrd or legacy mboxo. Ctime-style From separators are required. mboxrd removes one quote from recursively quoted From body lines; mboxo removes a single quote only and cannot distinguish a literal >From line. Choose the actual export format; automatic variant detection is unavailable. MSF indexes, SBD directory trees, whole profiles, EML, Maildir and Content-Length mboxcl/mboxcl2 are unsupported. No directories are scanned, source files changed, provider writes issued, mail uploaded, or automatic rules/AI/replies/bot actions triggered. Morrow makes private snapshots and rejects a source changed or replaced while copying. Resume verifies the entire saved snapshot before using committed offsets, independently of later changes to the original export. Complete MIME, original headers/dates, parsed text/HTML, decoding warnings and binary/inline attachments stay in durable Local Folders for offline reading, search and original EML export through the existing reader sanitizer and remote-image policy. Exact de-framed bytes determine duplicate identity per original destination; Message-ID alone does not merge messages. Identical imports skip their original receipt even after local moves; different destinations and different line endings or headers remain distinct. Thunderbird read/star/reply/forward flags are mapped, deleted entries are skipped, Partial entries fail as incomplete, queued/draft metadata stays inert, and other tags/profile settings are not imported. Results show imported, total skipped, duplicate, Thunderbird-deleted and failed counts. Moved originals stay in their current folders and can be found by subject or message text in Local Folders search. The selected saved job shows its current status. Completed jobs, including those with errors, can open the recorded original destination when that folder is still available. Counts and input offsets commit atomically with complete mail and attachments. Stop or Escape cancels outstanding parsing and remaining messages, retaining prior commits. Restart never resumes work automatically. Continue re-verifies snapshots and resumes after the last durable boundary. Parsing failures and oversized entries are counted separately when boundaries are known; ambiguous separators, oversized lines/headers, unsupported framing and read/storage failures stop without guessing. Failed input remains in private snapshots. The latest 100 jobs and first 50 failure offsets per job are shown. Limits: 100 GiB input per job, 32 MiB per original message, 256 KiB per line/header block, 256 attachments / 32 MiB decoded attachment bytes, 20 seconds / 256 MiB V8 old-generation limit per MIME worker. Streaming uses 64 KiB reads, one message and one worker at a time. Each run pauses after 512 MiB committed input or 10 minutes; snapshot creation or verification that exceeds 10 minutes needs a smaller export. SQLite/checksums remain synchronous; memory/latency are bounded by message size, not certified native frame times. Private snapshots need additional disk space and stay until the explicit Remove snapshots review; that action preserves original sources and saved mail but ends recovery for failed input. Back up local-folders.sqlite with Morrow stopped, plus mbox-imports if retaining import recovery. There is no import CLI/bot command. Native Windows/macOS dialogs, live Thunderbird profiles, real power loss and screen-reader behavior remain unverified by synthetic checks.
